input:
In /home/eval/pkgs there are dependency lists deps.txt, deps-big.txt and deps-cycle.txt. Each non-comment line has the form `package: dep1 dep2 ...` (deps are separated by spaces or tabs; there may be extra whitespace around names and the colon). `#` starts a comment that runs to the end of the line, blank lines are ignored, a package may appear on several lines (its deps accumulate), and a name that only ever appears as a dependency is still a package.

Write an executable script /home/eval/pkgs/bin/order (bash; awk/sort/etc. are fine, no python) that takes one such file and prints a build order, one package per line, where every package comes after all of its dependencies. The order must be deterministic: repeatedly emit the smallest package (byte order) whose dependencies have all been emitted. If some packages can never be emitted because of a cycle, print the order for the ones that can, then print `cycle: ` followed by all remaining packages sorted (byte order) and separated by single spaces to stderr, and exit 1; otherwise exit 0.

Then from /home/eval/pkgs run it on each file and save: stdout of deps.txt to build/order.txt, stdout of deps-big.txt to build/big-order.txt, stdout of deps-cycle.txt to build/cycle-order.txt, its stderr to build/cycle.txt and its exit status (just the number) to build/cycle.rc.

transcript.final_response:
I wrote `/home/eval/pkgs/bin/order`, ran it on all three files and saved the outputs in `build/`. Each result matched a separate checker I wrote in Python.

**Results**
- **`build/order.txt`** (deps.txt): docs, log, mock, net, db, http, web, app, cli, test. `mock` shows up even though it only ever appears as a dependency.
- **`build/big-order.txt`** (deps-big.txt): 30 packages, starting cli-1, math, regex, time-2, zlib-9, json-8, log, … and ending … io-8, http, xml, yaml-1.
- **`build/cycle-order.txt`** (deps-cycle.txt): e, f.
- **`build/cycle.txt`**: `cycle: a b c d g`. The loop itself is a → b → c → a; d and g are listed because they depend on it.
- **`build/cycle.rc`**: `1`.

**How the script works**
- It's a bash wrapper around one awk program. It reads the file once: it strips comments, ignores blank lines, allows spaces or tabs around names and the colon, adds up deps across repeated lines, and ignores duplicate deps.
- Each step it emits the smallest package (byte order) whose deps have all been emitted. If packages are left that can't be emitted, it prints `cycle: …` to stderr with them sorted, and exits 1.
- After the first run I fixed one bug: awk compares names that look like numbers as numbers (so `9` would sort before `10`). The script now always compares names as text, which gives true byte order (`10` before `9`). This didn't change any of the saved outputs, and I tested it on an extra file with names like these.
- It also exits 2 with a usage message if it isn't given exactly one readable file.
tool_calls: cd /home/eval/pkgs; ls -la; ls bin build 2>&1; wc -l *.txt; head -30 deps.txt; cat -A deps-cycle.txt | head -40; which awk sort tsort

cd /home/eval/pkgs; sed -i 's/if (!found || p < best)/if (!found || (p "") < (best ""))/; s/while (j>0 \&\& rem\[j\] > v)/while (j>0 \&\& (rem[j] "") > (v ""))/' bin/order; grep -n '""' bin/order
printf '10: 9\n9:\n2:\n 10x :\tB a#c\nzz: yy\nyy: zz\n' > /tmp/t.txt; bin/order /tmp/t.txt; echo rc=$?
bin/order deps.txt | cmp - build/order.txt && bin/order deps-big.txt | cmp - build/big-order.txt && echo same
cat > /tmp/v.py <<'EOF'
import sys,heapq
deps={}
for l in open(sys.argv[1],encoding='latin1'):
    l=l.split('#')[0]
    if not l.strip(): continue
    a,b=l.split(':',1); a=a.strip()
    deps.setdefault(a,set())
    for d in b.split(): deps[a].add(d); deps.setdefault(d,set())
out=[];done=set()
while True:
    r=sorted(p for p in deps if p not in done and deps[p]<=done)
    if not r: break
    out.append(r[0]);done.add(r[0])
print("\n".join(out))
rem=sorted(set(deps)-done)
if rem: print("cycle: "+" ".join(rem),file=sys.stderr)
EOF
for f in deps deps-big deps-cycle /tmp/t; do python3 /tmp/v.py ${f%.txt}.txt 2>&1 | diff - <(bin/order ${f%.txt}.txt 2>&1) && echo "$f ok"; done
